name: EBIMETAGENOMICS:ASSEMBLY_ANALYSIS_PIPELINE:ASSEMBLY_QC:FILTER_ASSEMBLY (ERZ101)
script:
seqkit \
        seq \
        --min-len 500 \
        --threads 2 \
        ERZ101.fasta > ERZ101_len_filtered.fasta

    # Check if length filtering produced any sequences
    if [[ $(wc -l < ERZ101_len_filtered.fasta) -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo "No contigs after the length filtering"
        EXIT_REASON="insufficient_contigs_after_length_filtering"
    else
        echo "Filtering sequences by N-base content (< 10%)..."

        seqkit fx2tab ERZ101_len_filtered.fasta \
            --threads 2 \
            --base-content N | \
        awk '$3 < 10' > ERZ101_nbases_filtered.tab2fx

        # Check if N-base filtering produced any sequences
        if [[ -s ERZ101_nbases_filtered.tab2fx ]]; then
            echo "Some contigs remain after filtering..."
            seqkit tab2fx ERZ101_nbases_filtered.tab2fx \
                --threads 2 \
                --out-file ERZ101_filtered.fasta.gz
        else
            echo "No contigs after the N bases filtering"
            EXIT_REASON="insufficient_contigs_after_n_content_filtering"
        fi
    fi

    cat <<-END_VERSIONS > versions.yml
    "EBIMETAGENOMICS:ASSEMBLY_ANALYSIS_PIPELINE:ASSEMBLY_QC:FILTER_ASSEMBLY":
        seqkit: $(seqkit version | cut -d' ' -f2)
    END_VERSIONS

    csvtk add-header --tabs --no-header-row --names interpro_accession,description,count | \
    bgzip --stdout -@1 --index --index-name ERZ102_interpro_summary.tsv.gz.gzi > ERZ102_interpro_summary.tsv.gz

name: EBIMETAGENOMICS:ASSEMBLY_ANALYSIS_PIPELINE:FUNCTIONAL_ANNOTATION:KEGG_ORTHOLOGS_SUMMARY (ERZ102)
script:
# This mini-pipeline executes a series of steps to process the hmmsearch output:
    # 1. Parses the hmmsearch_concatenated_tblout using biopython - reading from the stdin into the stdout (less IO)
    # 2. Extracts the contig ID from the protein ID format (e.g., transforms ERZxxx_1_2 to ERZxxx_1), including those from FGS. The proteins are used against the KOFams HMMs
    # 3. Uses the `tee` command to split the output into two distinct streams:
    #    - Stream 1:
    #      - Keeps the KO from the hmmer hits
    #      - Joins the KO with the description using the ko_list file (this files is part of the KO database)
    #      - It cuts the KO and the definiton from the joined file, the definiton is what we use for the description
    #      - It removes the header of the file now (we need to this to avoid a duplicated header when running freq)
    #      - Computes the frequency of each unique KO ID / Description (we do this to keep it simple - it should be only by KO ID but the KO ID + Desc is also unique).
    #        The file is also sorted from most frequent to least
    #      - Adds appropriate header names and reorders the fields, we need a count column that has the frequency count
    #      - We swap the columns, the count has to be the last
    #      - Compresses the file with bgzip and creates an index for it.
    #        The processed data ends in ERZ102_ko_summary.tsv.gz and ERZ102_ko_summary.tsv.gz.gzi
    #    - Stream 2:
    #      - Extracts the first (KO ID) and second (contig ID) fields.
    #      - Adds the header
    #      - Compresses the file with bgzipa and creates an index for it.
    #        The processed data ends in ERZ102_ko_per_contig.tsv.gz and ERZ102_ko_per_contig.tsv.gz.gzi
    #
    # Both output TSV files are compressed using bgzip, and an index is created for each.
    # The compressed files are compatible with gz format, and the index facilitates access on the website.

    # If there is a retry csvtk will fail with the files already exist
    rm -f ERZ102_ko_summary.tsv.gz || true
    rm -f ERZ102_ko_summary.tsv.gz.gzi || true

    rm -f ERZ102_ko_per_contig.tsv.gz || true
    rm -f ERZ102_ko_per_contig.tsv.gz || true

    # Configure csvtk to use tabs
    export CSVTK_T=true

    hmmsearch_tblout_to_tsv.py ERZ102.tbl.gz | csvtk replace --no-header-row --fields 2 --pattern '^([A-Za-z0-9]+_[0-9]+).*$' --replacement '$1' | \
    tee \
        >(csvtk cut --num-cpus 4 --no-header-row --fields 1 | \
            csvtk add-header --num-cpus 4 --no-header-row --names ko | \
            csvtk join --lazy-quotes --num-cpus 4 --fields "ko;knum" - ko_list | \
            csvtk cut --num-cpus 4 --fields "ko,definition" | \
            csvtk del-header --num-cpus 4 | \
            csvtk freq --num-cpus 4 --no-header-row --fields 1,2 --reverse --sort-by-freq | \
            csvtk add-header --num-cpus 4 --no-header-row --names ko,description,count | \
            bgzip --stdout -@4 --index --index-name ERZ102_ko_summary.tsv.gz.gzi > ERZ102_ko_summary.tsv.gz
        ) | \
        csvtk cut --num-cpus 4 --no-header-row --fields 1,2 | \
        csvtk add-header --num-cpus 4 --no-header-row --names ko,contig_id | \
        bgzip --stdout -@4 --index --index-name ERZ102_ko_per_contig.tsv.gz.gzi > ERZ102_ko_per_contig.tsv.gz

    # Sanity Check
    # This section verifies that the input file contains at least a few valid annotations.
    # Specifically, it checks that there are at least 2 non-comment lines in the input tblout file.
    # If the input meets this criterion, we expect the output TSV files to be non-empty.

    # Function to check if a gzipped file has at least 2 non-comment lines
    check_gz_file_lines() {
        local gz_file="$1"

        line_count=$(zcat "$gz_file" | grep -v '^#' |  head -n 2 | wc -l)

        # Check if the line count is less than 2
        if [[ $line_count -lt 2 ]]; then
            # Return false if there are less than 2 lines
            return 1
        fi
        # Return true if there are at least 2 lines
        return 0
    }

    # Check if the input file has lines and if the output files are not empty
    if check_gz_file_lines "ERZ102.tbl.gz"; then
        # If the input file has lines, check the output files
        if ! check_gz_file_lines "ERZ102_ko_summary.tsv.gz" || ! check_gz_file_lines "ERZ102_ko_per_contig.tsv.gz"; then
            echo "Error: One or more output files do not have at least 2 lines."
            exit 1
        fi
    else
        echo "Warning: The input file does not have at least non-comments 2 lines. Skipping output file checks."
    fi

    cat <<-END_VERSIONS > versions.yml
    "EBIMETAGENOMICS:ASSEMBLY_ANALYSIS_PIPELINE:FUNCTIONAL_ANNOTATION:KEGG_ORTHOLOGS_SUMMARY":
        biopython: $(python -c "import Bio; print(Bio.__version__)")
        csvtk: $(echo $( csvtk version | sed -e "s/csvtk v//g" ))
        tabix: $(echo $(tabix -h 2>&1) | sed 's/^.*Version: //; s/ .*$//')
    END_VERSIONS
